fields.description: Pipeline column: one of the team's statuses (status-taxonomy.yml). Free text; an unusual value is advisory.
Document type. story, bug and spike make the file a pipeline story; any other value, or none, keeps it a plain document.
Story ids this story depends on. Each must resolve; drives the dependency graph.
Free-form tags, for example [infra, urgent].
Relative paths to supporting documents. A path that is not found is advisory.
The story's display id, for example W-5. Unique within an org.
The repo the story's code lives in, as owner/repo. Must be a configured repo: resolve it with list_source_repos, never invent it.
Optional. The repo whose history holds the story's work when that is not source_repo, as owner/repo (for example the context repo); story_changes reads it.
Legacy. Read only as a fallback on older documents; use branch.
Legacy. Read only as a fallback on older documents; use branch.
The team the document belongs to. If set, it must be a configured team.
Epics: the repos the epic spans, as owner/repo.
Stories: the story's branch, used to create its worktree. Epics: the integration branch (by default integration/ followed by the epic id).
The sprint the story belongs to, for example 2026-08-A.
Estimate in points. A non-numeric value is ignored; a value off the scale 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13 is advisory.
Who the story is assigned to (a username). A login missing from the org roster is advisory.
Order within a board column. The board writes it; you rarely set it by hand.
A standalone document's automation subject id, which makes a plain document an addressable automation subject. A story uses story_id instead.
The story's title. Without it, Markdown uses the first # heading and HTML uses the title tag or the first h1.
The id of the epic the story belongs to. Without it, the epic folder on the story's path counts.
Alias of parent_epic, read when parent_epic is absent.
Priority, p0 (highest) to p4. Sorting also ranks words such as critical, high, medium and low.
